title: A Portrait for the Alibi
premise: Oscar Voss, a night-shift taxi dispatcher who has quietly solved three deaths the police dismissed as accidents, is hired by a nervous client named Miriam Kade to prove that her brother Elias has not yet been murdered — only that he will be, on a date circled in an old family ledger. As Oscar traces the threat through alibis stitched together thirty years ago around a fire at the Kade family boathouse, he discovers the 'alibi' was never proof of innocence but a shared pact of silence among five survivors. When Elias vanishes two days before the marked date, Oscar must decide whether to finally step out of the shadows and expose himself to the police he's outsmarted for years. In the end, Oscar saves Elias by forcing the truth of the fire into the open — learning that his own mother was the sixth person in the boathouse that night, and that his lifelong invisibility was inherited from her escape.
about_author: Xanthe Ishikawa is the pen name of a former night-shift radio operator who spent eleven years listening to a city talk itself to sleep before turning those voices into fiction. They write mysteries about people who watch carefully and are watched too late.

chapters.title: The Frequency of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Oscar Voss works the graveyard shift at Citywide Taxi, mapping the city through radio chatter and noticing what no one else does. A brief flashback establishes how he solved the drowning of a councilman without ever leaving his dispatch desk. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of being unseen.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Miriam Kade arrives at the depot at 3 a.m., paying triple for a strange job: prove her brother Elias hasn't been murdered yet. She shows Oscar a family ledger with a date circled six weeks out and a note reading 'one for each.' POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: intrigue sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Five Names, One Fire
chapters.summary: Oscar digs into the Kade family history and finds a 1994 boathouse fire officially ruled accidental, with five survivors who all provided each other's alibis. He maps their current lives: a judge, a restaurateur, a retired cop, a nun, and Elias himself. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the pattern-recognition thrill of a puzzle opening.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Oscar confronts Miriam about the ledger's missing sixth entry; she goes pale and denies there ever was one. Meanwhile Elias refuses to meet, insisting through a locked door that the past should stay buried. POV: Oscar, with a short Miriam interlude. Emotional beat: first fracture in the client relationship.

chapters.title: The Judge's Perfect Evening
chapters.summary: Oscar surveils Judge Ada Renner-Kade and finds her alibi for the fire night is airtight — almost suspiciously so, rehearsed like testimony. A tail car follows Oscar home for the first time in years. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the watcher realizing he can be watched.

chapters.title: Smoke Memory
chapters.summary: Sister Brigid, the nun survivor, agrees to talk and describes the fire in sensory detail that contradicts the official report — the doors were barred from outside. She begs Oscar to stop before someone keeps the ledger's promise. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: dread replacing curiosity.

chapters.title: A Death That Hasn't Happened
chapters.summary: Oscar reconstructs how the murder will occur: Elias's medication is being swapped batch by batch, a slow untraceable poisoning timed for the circled date. He realizes the killer needs an accomplice inside the pharmacy chain. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: horror at solving a crime still in progress.

chapters.title: The Retired Cop's Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Ex-cop Dale Mercer, dying of cancer, leaves Oscar a tape admitting he falsified the fire report — but claims he did it to protect someone whose name he refuses to say on record. The tape ends mid-sentence. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief and frustration at a truth that dies with its keeper.

chapters.title: Invisible Man, Visible Trail
chapters.summary: Oscar's careful anonymity starts failing: his landlord is questioned, his dispatch logs subpoenaed by someone with a warrant signed by Judge Renner-Kade. Detective Ilsa Brandt, who once suspected him in the earlier cases, reappears. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the price of survival coming due.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibi
chapters.summary: Oscar lays out the timeline and sees it: every survivor's life pivoted on the same week in 1994 — promotions, inheritances, vocations — as if bought with silence. The restaurant owner, Tomas Kade, hosts a reunion dinner for the survivors. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: cold clarity about complicity.

chapters.title: Dinner with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Oscar infiltrates the reunion as a substitute driver and overhears the survivors rehearsing a new, coordinated story — they know the date is coming, and they've chosen a scapegoat. It isn't any of them. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: revulsion at watching an alibi being woven live.

chapters.title: Elias Runs
chapters.summary: Elias flees his home, convinced the date marks his death, and calls Oscar from a payphone — the only man he trusts because he owes him nothing. He reveals the ledger counts victims, not years: one per decade since the fire. POV: alternating Oscar and Elias. Emotional beat: desperate alliance formed.

chapters.title: Detective Brandt's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ilsa Brandt corners Oscar, presenting evidence he faked his earlier 'solutions' to feed his own ego. Instead of denying it, Oscar offers her the pharmacy swap trail — forcing an uneasy, deniable partnership. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: grudging respect between natural enemies.

chapters.title: The Sixth Name
chapters.summary: In the burned ledger's carbon copy hidden in Sister Brigid's convent, Oscar finds a sixth name smudged but legible: V. Voss. His mother, Lena Voss, listed as deceased in 1994 — the year she vanished from his childhood. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of his own history.

chapters.title: My Mother's Alibi
chapters.summary: Oscar tears through records and learns Lena was the boathouse caretaker, blamed for barring the door, and that the five survivors' pact was to bury her name along with the fire. Her 'death' was the price of his safety. POV: Oscar, raw first-person confession passages. Emotional beat: betrayal and terrible understanding.

chapters.title: One for Each Decade
chapters.summary: Oscar decodes the ledger fully: a victim every ten years — 2004, 2014, and now 2024 — each death disguised as accident, each covered by the same five alibis. The previous two victims were people who had tried to talk. Elias is next because he found the carbons. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the scale of the silence revealed.

chapters.title: The Pharmacist's Window
chapters.summary: Brandt and Oscar trace the tampered medication to a small-town pharmacist who confesses to being blackmailed over his own thirty-year-old secret: he drove the car that blocked the fire exit. The conspiracy is wider than five. POV: alternating Oscar and the pharmacist. Emotional beat: cowardice recognized as contagious.

chapters.title: Circled Date
chapters.summary: Two days before the marked date, Elias disappears from the safehouse. Miriam, wracked with guilt, admits she hired Oscar not to save her brother but to give herself an alibi for whatever happened — she's the inside accomplice. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: trust collapsing into ash.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Rebuilt
chapters.summary: Oscar deduces the killers will stage Elias's death at the rebuilt boathouse — symmetry as signature. He and Brandt arrive to find the doors barred from outside again, history repeating its exact shape, with the judge presiding over the scene like a verdict. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: terror and fury converging.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Climax. Oscar broadcasts the whole night on the open taxi dispatch frequency — every driver, every scanner, the city itself as witness — while going in through the water gate his mother once used. He pulls Elias out as the survivors' pact shatters under public exposure. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: invisibility sacrificed for a life.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Fallout: arrests, the judge's resignation, Miriam's plea deal, and Brandt formally closing the 1994 case with Lena Voss's name restored to the record — alive until proven otherwise. Oscar gives his first-ever statement under his real name. POV: Ilsa, then Oscar. Emotional beat: the exhausting relief of being seen.

chapters.title: Day Shift
chapters.summary: Months later, Oscar takes a day job training new dispatchers and receives a postcard postmarked from a coastal town, unsigned, in handwriting that matches the ledger's margins. He doesn't chase it; he pins it above his desk. Some survivals deserve their silence. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: belonging found in staying findable.
